title: NASA selects successor to CAPSTONE lunar mission
summary: NASA has chosen Advanced Space to lead a follow-up mission to CAPSTONE, which will demonstrate rendezvous and proximity operations in cislunar space. The new mission aims to further test lunar navigation and operational techniques.

title: Upper C-band auction offers another lift for GEO industry
summary: The FCC's upcoming upper C-band spectrum auction is expected to generate over $6 billion, benefiting satellite operators and funding new geostationary spacecraft and transition costs.

title: Sphinx Defense wins $287 million contract for strategic satellite communications software
summary: Sphinx Defense has secured a $287 million contract to develop mission planning software for the ESS next-generation strategic communications satellites. This award highlights the growing demand for advanced satellite communications solutions in the defense sector.

title: Orbes unveils Exo-ORB and agreement with Symphony Space
summary: Orbes introduced Exo-ORB, a free-flying satellite, and announced an agreement with Symphony Space to capture imagery of an uncrewed Symphony Space station. The collaboration aims to support future space station operations.

title: Intel debuts new chip for space computing
summary: Intel has introduced a new chip named Starfire designed for space computing, enabling onboard data processing and AI workloads. This development highlights Intel's expansion into the space technology sector.

title: SpaceNews Welcomes Max Aliprandi as Business Development Associate
summary: SpaceNews announced the hiring of Max Aliprandi as Business Development Associate to strengthen its sales and business development teams. This move supports the company's expansion efforts and audience growth.

title: Amazon files application for direct-to-device satellite constellation
summary: Amazon has submitted an application to the FCC for a constellation of over 5,100 satellites to provide direct-to-device services using Globalstar spectrum. This move aims to expand Amazon's satellite connectivity offerings.

title: Blue Origin to test New Glenn upper stages at Stennis
summary: Blue Origin will conduct tests on New Glenn upper stages at NASA's Stennis Space Center. The company is also rebuilding its Cape Canaveral launch complex.

title: Rocket Lab to open Alaska launch site under $266 million Space Force deal
summary: Rocket Lab will establish a new launch site in Alaska under a $266 million contract with the U.S. Space Force. The facility will support up to 18 suborbital missions for military testing.

title: BALLS on the moon: China set to launch Africa's 1st lunar science mission in 2029
summary: China is set to launch Africa's first lunar science mission in 2029, involving three spherical probes to the moon's south pole aboard the Chang'e 8 lander. This mission marks a significant milestone for African space exploration.

title: Betelgeuse, Betelgeuse! Astronomers capture clearest image yet of famous star's elusive companion
summary: Astronomers have captured the clearest image yet of Betelgeuse's elusive companion star, revealing new insights into the famous red giant. The discovery is hailed as a significant moment in stellar observation.

title: 'Crazy idea' succeeds: Scientists monitor space junk with radio telescopes
summary: Scientists successfully monitored space junk using radio telescopes for the first time. This breakthrough could enhance tracking of debris in Earth's orbit.

title: The unique DJI Lito X1 drone is packed full of functionality and you can't buy it in the USA
summary: The DJI Lito X1 drone offers advanced features like omnidirectional obstacle sensing in a user-friendly design, but it is not available for purchase in the USA.

title: Starship in space! See highlights of SpaceX megarocket's epic Flight 13 test launch (video)
summary: SpaceX's Starship completed its 13th test flight with notable success and impressive visuals. The mission is part of ongoing development for the megarocket.

title: Rocket Lab to start launching missile-defense missions from Alaska under $266 million Space Force deal
summary: Rocket Lab has secured a $266 million contract with the U.S. Space Force to conduct up to 18 suborbital missile-defense launches, primarily from Alaska's Pacific Spaceport Complex.

title: On this day in space! July 27, 1962:  The 1st zero-g cosmonaut training flight took off on a Soviet jetliner
summary: On July 27, 1962, two Soviet cosmonauts conducted the first zero-gravity training flight on a jetliner to simulate weightlessness. This milestone was crucial for preparing humans for spaceflight.

title: Are we overlooking signs of alien life that aren't technological or biological? 'Bread would be a signature of intelligence'
summary: Scientists propose 'noosignatures' as a new method to detect alien life, suggesting that signs of intelligence like bread could indicate non-technological or non-biological alien activity. This concept bridges the gap between biosignatures and technosignatures in the search for extraterrestrial life.

title: We've found huge discounts on a range of ZWO astronomy cameras, including three we love
summary: B&H Photo Video is offering discounts on ZWO astronomy cameras and related astrophotography gear. This includes astrocams, telescopes, and mounts to enhance stargazing setups.

title: Smoke Blankets Oregon
summary: Lightning storms in central and eastern Oregon have sparked numerous wildfires, creating widespread smoke blankets across the region.

title: NASA Astronaut Chris Williams to Discuss Space Station Mission
summary: NASA astronaut Chris Williams will discuss his eight-month mission aboard the International Space Station during a news conference on August 4. The event will be streamed live from Johnson Space Center in Houston.

title: NASA Science Soars During August Total Solar Eclipse
summary: NASA will study the Sun's corona during the August 12 total solar eclipse, which will pass over Greenland and Iceland. This event provides a rare opportunity to gather new scientific data about the Sun's outer atmosphere and its effects on Earth.

title: NASA Astronaut Chris Williams Returns to Earth
summary: NASA astronaut Chris Williams returned to Earth on July 26, 2026, after completing his first mission aboard the International Space Station. He spent eight months supporting scientific investigations and technology demonstrations during Expedition 74.

title: NASA’s Swift Sees ‘Wandering’ Mega Black Hole Shredding Star
summary: NASA's Neil Gehrels Swift Observatory detected a rare 'wandering' mega black hole shredding a star outside a galaxy's core. This is the first time such an event has been observed so far from a galaxy's center.

title: NASA to Cover Three US Spacewalks, Host Preview News Conference
summary: NASA announced coverage for three upcoming US spacewalks in August 2026 to upgrade solar arrays, replace a communications antenna, and connect power and data cables. The spacewalks will be broadcast with a preview news conference to discuss the activities.

title: NASA’s Hubble Shows Star Formation in Andromeda Galaxy Winding Down
summary: NASA's Hubble Space Telescope has observed that star formation in the Andromeda Galaxy has significantly declined over the past 500 million years. This discovery provides new insights into the galaxy's evolution and future star formation trends.

title: NASA Astronaut Chris Williams, Crewmates Return from Space Station
summary: NASA astronaut Chris Williams and two Roscosmos cosmonauts concluded an eight-month science mission aboard the International Space Station and returned to Earth with a safe landing in Kazakhstan.

title: NASA’s ESCAPADE Snaps Family Portrait of Earth, Moon
summary: NASA's ESCAPADE spacecraft captured images of Earth and the Moon during its journey to Mars. The photos were taken from a distance of 363,250 miles from Earth and 115,600 miles from the Moon.

title: New Crew Members Welcomed to International Space Station
summary: Three new crew members—Anna Kikina and Pyotr Dubrov of Roscosmos, and Anil Menon of NASA—arrived at the International Space Station on July 14, 2026, after launching from the Baikonur Cosmodrome. They were welcomed aboard the ISS on July 18, 2026, and celebrated with a cake.

title: Launch Preview: Falcon 9 and Chang Zheng rockets set to launch this week
summary: Five orbital launches are scheduled this week, including a Chang Zheng 6A rocket in China. SpaceX's Falcon 9 is also among the planned launches.

title: Juno reveals surprising subsurface tempertures at Io, remarkably smooth surface
summary: NASA's Juno spacecraft reveals surprising subsurface temperatures and a remarkably smooth surface on Jupiter's moon Io during two recent flybys. The findings challenge previous assumptions about the volcanic moon's geology.

title: Blue Origin to conduct New Glenn second stage hot fires on Stennis B-2 stand
summary: NASA and Blue Origin have finalized plans to hot-fire test the second stage of the New Glenn rocket on the Stennis B-2 test stand. This marks a significant step in preparing the vehicle for its upcoming launch.

title: Starship Flight 13 achieves new firsts for SpaceX
summary: Starship Flight 13, featuring Booster 20 and Ship 40, achieved new milestones during its third attempt. The launch marked another step forward for SpaceX's Starship program.

title: Soyuz MS-29 crew arrives at ISS, U.S. EVA completes Canadarm2 repairs
summary: The Soyuz MS-29 crew successfully arrived at the International Space Station (ISS), expanding the station's crew by three members. A U.S. extravehicular activity (EVA) completed repairs on the Canadarm2 robotic arm.

title: Path to Starship Flight 13 requires additional Booster 20 test
summary: SpaceX is preparing for Starship Flight 13, targeting a launch no earlier than July 23, but requires additional testing of Booster 20. The delay highlights ongoing technical challenges in the Starship program.

title: Falcon 9 to launch MRV-1 robotic servicing spacecraft for Northrop Grumman
summary: SpaceX's Falcon 9 is scheduled to launch the MRV-1 robotic servicing spacecraft for Northrop Grumman from Florida. The Mission Robotic Vehicle (MRV-1) aims to demonstrate in-space servicing capabilities.

title: Launch Preview: Falcon 9, Starship, and Chinese rockets scheduled to launch
summary: SpaceX is preparing for a new launch attempt of Starship Flight 13 after a previous abort. Additionally, Falcon 9 and Chinese rockets are also scheduled for launches.

title: Making Progress: Relativity’s Terran R, Rocket Lab’s Neutron, and PLD Space’s Miura 5
summary: Three companies—Relativity Space, Rocket Lab, and PLD Space—are making progress on their respective launch vehicles: Terran R, Neutron, and Miura 5. While Starship's test program has dominated recent attention, these developments highlight advancements in the space industry.

title: China’s first recovered booster returns to port as LandSpace aims for first land recovery
summary: China achieved a milestone with the first successful recovery of a booster, and LandSpace is aiming for the first land recovery of a booster.

title: ESA Delivers: 50 years booklet
summary: The European Space Agency (ESA) released a booklet highlighting 50 major achievements over its 50-year history. The publication celebrates significant milestones and contributions to space exploration and science.

title: Meet space startups at ESA’s Industry Space Days
summary: ESA's Industry Space Days event on 16–17 September at ESA-ESTEC in the Netherlands will bring together startups and space industry leaders to exchange ideas, showcase capabilities, and explore collaboration opportunities.

title: The silicon brains steering next-generation antennas
summary: The article discusses advancements in silicon-based technology for next-generation antennas, highlighting innovations in the space industry. It emphasizes the role of silicon in enhancing antenna performance for future applications.

title: Plato's electronics ready for space
summary: ESA's PLATO spacecraft has completed electromagnetic compatibility tests in the Maxwell Test Chamber, confirming its electronics are ready for space. The mission is scheduled to launch on an Ariane 6 rocket in March 2027.

title: Test firing at brand new green chemical propulsion lab
summary: A new green chemical propulsion lab conducted its first test firing. This marks a significant step in developing environmentally friendly propulsion technologies for space missions.

title: Upcoming ESA–Industry events on CM25 implementation
summary: ESA is hosting a series of events to present the follow-up to the Council Meeting at Ministerial Level 2025 (CM25), focusing on planned activities, priorities, and industrial opportunities across ESA programs.

title: One robotic arm to rule them all
summary: The news discusses a significant advancement in robotic arm technology for space applications. It highlights a breakthrough that could revolutionize robotic operations in space.

title: We’re back: Proba-3 ready for more science
summary: The Proba-3 mission's Coronagraph spacecraft and ASPIICS instrument are fully operational, resuming formation flying to create artificial eclipses for scientific observations.

title: Amazon Joins the Direct-to-Device Race
summary: Amazon has entered the direct-to-device satellite market by filing an FCC request to launch 5,105 low-Earth orbit satellites. This move positions the company to compete in the growing space-based connectivity sector.

title: New Report Maps Potential Futures for Africa’s Space Ecosystem
summary: A new report explores potential future developments for Africa's space industry as the continent aims to establish itself as a major player in the global space sector. The analysis highlights opportunities and challenges for Africa's growing space ecosystem.

title: Rocket Lab Expands to Alaska with $266M Launch Contract
summary: Rocket Lab will establish a new launch site at the Pacific Spaceport Complex-Alaska (PSCA) in Kodiak with launches starting by the end of this year. The expansion is supported by a $266 million launch contract.

title: ORBES Unveils Exo-ORB Maintenance Spacecraft
summary: ORBES introduced the Exo-ORB Maintenance Spacecraft, a 12U, sub-26-kg spacecraft designed for inspection missions. The spacecraft is intended to launch onboard customer infrastructure for ready-to-use operations.

title: Starship Sticks the Water Landing on Flight 13
summary: SpaceX successfully conducted the 13th test flight of its Starship rocket, achieving its first intact water landing. The mission marks a significant milestone in the rocket's development.

title: ESA Puts €65M Behind Europe’s First Lunar Ice Rover
summary: ESA has committed €65 million to support Europe's first lunar polar ice exploration rover mission, led by ispace-Europe. The funding marks a significant step toward lunar exploration and resource utilization.

title: Lunar Outpost Plans to Fly NVIDIA Chips to the Moon
summary: Lunar Outpost is planning to send NVIDIA chips to the Moon, highlighting the intersection of the semiconductor industry and lunar exploration efforts. This move underscores the growing importance of advanced computing technology in space missions.

title: A Deep Dive into the Bluetooth Satellite Connectivity Market Following the FCC’s Proposal
summary: The FCC is proposing to open unlicensed Bluetooth and Wi-Fi frequencies for space-based communications. This move could significantly impact the Bluetooth satellite connectivity market.

title: FCC Filings Show Eutelsat is Working on a New 528-sat Constellation Beyond OneWeb
summary: Eutelsat is developing a new constellation of 528 satellites, separate from its OneWeb operations. The company indicates that the Next program is still in development.

title: NASA Puts $2B Price Tag on Nuclear Mars Mission
summary: NASA has estimated a $2 billion cost for the Space Reactor-1 Freedom, a fission-powered spacecraft designed for interplanetary missions to Mars. This mission marks the first use of nuclear propulsion for deep space exploration.

title: Space-Based Data Centers: Inside the Race to Move Compute to Orbit
summary: The space industry is exploring the concept of space-based data centers to address the growing demand for computing power driven by AI, with recent months seeing increased interest and activity in this area.

title: SES Space & Defense Wins Space Station Connectivity Deal With Starlab
summary: SES Space & Defense has partnered with Starlab to develop a communication architecture for continuous space station connectivity. The collaboration aims to enhance data transmission and operational efficiency for Starlab's space station.

title: Amazon Leo Files for 5,105 Satellites in Globalstar Spectrum for D2D
summary: Amazon has filed with the FCC to launch a Direct-to-Device satellite constellation of up to 5,105 satellites, utilizing spectrum from a planned acquisition of Globalstar. This move aims to expand Amazon's satellite communications capabilities.

title: SES Set to Receive $5.6B in Incentive Payments for C-Band Clearing
summary: SES is set to receive $5.6 billion in incentive payments from the FCC for clearing the C-band, while Eutelsat will receive $504 million as part of the final C-band clearing process.

title: Via Satellite Rising Stars of 2026
summary: Via Satellite announces its third annual class of 25 Rising Stars, highlighting young professionals shaping the future of the space and satellite industry.

title: Building the Connectivity Backbone for the Next Era of Lunar Exploration
summary: The article discusses the development of a connectivity backbone to support future lunar exploration efforts. It highlights the expansion of space-based services from Earth to the Moon.

title: How Fast Can You Build a Satellite? Inside the Smallsat Manufacturing Market
summary: The article discusses the challenges of small satellite manufacturing, highlighting the classic project management constraints of good, fast, and cheap, with an added focus on flexibility in the space industry. It explores the dynamics of the smallsat market and its unique demands.

title: Thermodynamics Does Not Care About Your Form Factor
summary: A spacecraft program faces challenges when addressing thermal management, as heat dissipation becomes a critical issue after structural and electronic components are already in place. The article emphasizes the importance of thermal design in spacecraft development.

title: In the AI Era, Constellations Emerge As a New Strategic Class of Assets
summary: The article discusses how AI is transforming military space operations, shifting focus from a few large satellites to constellations as a new strategic asset class. It highlights the increasing importance of satellite networks in reconnaissance and secure communications.

title: 10 Smallsat Startups to Watch in 2026
summary: Via Satellite has released its annual list of 10 smallsat startups to watch in 2026, highlighting early-stage companies (Series A or earlier) globally. These startups are in the initial funding phases and show potential in the small satellite industry.
